title: Home page Lights tab: one card per room

steps.headline: Which card layout makes switching, dimming and changing a room's lights simplest on the Lights tab?
steps.notice: Each room is now ONE card named like "Destin's Room Lights", with All off, the scenes button and a fold arrow in its header. Destin's Room is open; the unreachable TV backlight sits last.
steps.risk: All three keep what you decided: cards and colour menus start closed, scenes behind the palette button, the slider handle stays attached.

variants.label: Today
variants.summary: The Lights tab as it is now: a room card with a Lights card nested inside it.
variants.risk: Two cards for one room; the room name and "Lights" are separate headings.

variants.label: Room strip
variants.summary: One card per room, called "Destin's Room Lights". A big brightness bar for the whole room sits on top, with an All off button; open the card and each light is a slim row with its own thin bar and colour dot.
variants.risk: Slim rows are small to hit on a phone, and every light still needs its bar dragged precisely.

variants.label: Tile grid
variants.summary: One card per room. Under the room bar each light is a square tile: tap to switch it, drag it sideways to dim it, and its fill shows how bright it is. The coloured dot opens its colours.
variants.risk: Tap and drag share one surface, so a slow, wobbly tap can dim a light instead of switching it; drag is not discoverable until tried.

variants.label: Mixer
variants.summary: One card per room. Each light is a tall fader standing side by side like a sound desk, with the whole-room fader first. The bulb on top switches a light; the dot underneath opens its colours.
variants.risk: Looks the most different from the rest of the page; with many lights it wraps to a second row.

steps.headline: Does each layout still work at phone width?
steps.notice: The same open room on a 390 px wide screen.
steps.risk: The mixer wraps onto a second row; the title can take two lines.

steps.headline: When you first open the Lights tab, which closed cards are the clearest?
steps.notice: Every card starts closed: its name, how many are on, All off, scenes and the room bar (the mixer shows no bar until opened).
steps.risk: A closed card hides the individual lights, so switching one light takes an extra press.

steps.headline: Where do unreachable lights and rooms end up?
steps.notice: Here the whole Living Room is unreachable: its card drops to the end of the tab, greyed, and its All on button is off. Inside Destin's Room the unreachable TV backlight is last.
steps.risk: A room that comes back on moves back up on the next refresh.
